title: Function Basics: Domain & Range
author: 6950188c02683943243678c3
chapter_outcomes: Recognise the following function types from the shape of their graphs: a) linear, quadratic, cubic, reciprocal, exponential, trignometric
Determine one or two of coefficients of the variables or constants for the function types above
Determine values in a function from its graph

Use a graphic display calculator to: (a) sketch the graph of a function, (b) produce a table of values, (c) plot points, (d) find zeros, local maxima or local minima, (e) find the intersection of the graphs of functions, (f) find the vertex of a quadratic
Understand functions, domain and range and use function notation
Form composite functions as defined by $\text{gf}(x)=\text{g(f(}x))$
Find a quadratic function given: (a) vertex and another point, (b) $x$-intercepts and a point, (c) vertex or $x$-intercepts in the case where $a = 1$. Note: $y=a(x-h)^2+k$ has a vertex of $(h,k)$.
Understand the concept of asymptotes and identify simple examples parallel to the axes on a graph
Describe and identify transformations to a graph of $y = f(x)$ when $y = f(x) + k$ or $y = f(x + k)$, where $k$ is an integer.

Understand and use: the logarithmic function as the inverse of the exponential function, $y = a^x$ as equivalent to $x = \log_a y,$ the solution to $a^x = b$ as $x =\frac{\log b}{\log a}$. Noting that all logs will be base 10 unless otherwise stated.
